stem: An industrial engineering study measures the assembly time (seconds) for a sample of 15 factory workers. The sample mean is 64.2 sec with a sample standard deviation of 16.3 sec. However, 3 of the 15 observations appear to be outliers (values more than 2.5 standard deviations from the mean). If these outliers are removed, the remaining 12 observations have a mean of 62.2 sec and standard deviation of 11.3 sec. Estimate the true population mean and provide a 95% confidence interval that accounts for the uncertainty about whether outliers should be included.

ground_truth.answer: With all data: mean = 64.2, 95% CI = [55.2, 73.2]. Without outliers: mean = 62.2, 95% CI = [55.7, 68.7]. Combined interval accounting for analytic uncertainty: [55.2, 73.2]. Point estimate: 63.2 sec.

solution_steps: The outlier treatment choice creates structural uncertainty. Combined interval: [55.2, 73.2].
common_failure_modes: Using only the full sample without considering outlier impact
Removing outliers without reporting both analyses
Not recognizing that the choice of analysis method is itself a source of uncertainty
